huggingface/pybot.excerpt: # PyBot: can Python be a chatbot? / LLMs drive today’s chatbots and agents, but chatbots long predate them. Sixty years ago, ELIZA held conversations by matching patterns in what the user typed and answering with predefined templates. It could seem insightful, but its repertoire was narrow, and expanding it meant writing more rules by hand. How far could a rule-based chatbot go if a swarm of agents did that work instead? / We challenged a swarm of over 1,000 agents to build a chatbot entirely in Python: no weights, no training, just if-else branches, regex patterns and lookup tables. The agents wrote and evaluated over 5,000 versions, and the chatbot’s win rate on SmolTalkBench, where an LLM judge compares each reply with a reference answer, climbed from 0% to 26%. That puts it on par with SmolLM-360M-Instruct, which just a few years ago was state of the art for models under 1B parameters. / The result is PyBot: around 640k lines of code that can answer everyday questions, backed by 550k lines of tests the agents wrote themselves. / ## Try it out / Try PyBot in your terminal below, or in the browser on Hugging Face, where each reply shows which of PyBot’s modules produced it. / PyBot needs Python 3.8 or newer and nothing else: no packages to install and no model to download. / ```sh / git clone https://github.com/huggingface/pybot / cd pybot / python -m pybot / ``` / That starts a chat in your terminal: / ```text / ____        ____        __ / / __ \__  __/ __ )____  / /_ / / /_/ / / / / __  / __ \/ __/ / / ____/ /_/ / /_/ / /_/ / /_ / /_/    \__, /_____/\____/\__/ / /____/ / A chatbot written in plain Python. expo/exact.excerpt: # Exact / **The all-platform app framework. Agent native. Built for speed. No compromises.** / Exact is an **all-platform** framework for building real apps on the web, iOS, macOS, Android, and Linux — with Windows in active development, plus tvOS, watchOS, Android TV, and the terminal. / Exact is not a "cross-platform" framework. Cross-platform tools usually trade away each platform's strengths to maintain a lowest common denominator. Exact takes the opposite approach: build something **excellent on every platform on its own terms** — real DOM on the web, real UIKit on iOS, real AppKit on macOS, hardware-accelerated Material 3 rendering with native Android views on Android, and direct GPU/CPU rendering on Linux and Windows. Being **all-platform** is simply the side effect of getting every platform right from one source. / Everything in Exact is built around three priorities: / 1. **Agent Native** — Built from the ground up so coding agents can build, run, see, operate, and verify real apps on every platform through one deterministic loop. / 2. **Speed is King** — 100 ms cold starts, 100 ms edit-to-present reloads, zero app JavaScript before first pixel, and a ~20 KB web runtime, held to hard budgets. / 3. **No Compromises — Build Exactly What You Want** — Native platform controls with zero tells when you leave presentation unsaid; full creative control over layout, motion, graphics, shaders, and native platform objects whenever you want it. / > [!NOTE] / > Exact is pre-1.0 and changes daily. There is no packaged release, API stability guarantee, or backwards-compatibility layer yet — you build from a checkout of this repository. / Web / iOS / macOS / The browser's own DOM and CSS / UIKit views, native controls, and the system tab bar / AppKit views and native controls
